newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian politicians clash over Albanian shipwreck.
newsitem.headline: Italian politicians clash over Albanian shipwreck.

text.p: Italy searched for more victims of an Albanian shipwreck on Monday as politicians, worried about the reception of an imminent Italian-led mission to the impoverished state, argued over the tragedy.
Grieving survivors, who lost husbands, wives and young children in the disaster on Friday night, demanded answers from Rome. Tirana says around 80 people died in the incident.
"We want the truth," one man in the southern port of Brindisi told RAI television.

The navy, which has rejected accusations that it is to blame, said an aircraft was flying over a 30 mile area while the patrolling frigate "Zeffiro" was on the scene. Four bodies were recovered on Friday and 34 people rescued.
The small Albanian harbour patrol vessel crowded with refugees from the southern port of Vlore capsized and sank after colliding with a navy ship trying to turn it back.

Italian ships have been ordered by Rome to intercept Albanian boats heading for Italy and force them to turn back. Some 13,000 people have flooded into Italy in recent weeks and Italy maintains most fled for economic reasons.
The navy denies it is carrying out a formal blockade, saying patrols are engaged in dissuasive action.

Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, who interrupted his Easter vacation to fly to Brindisi on his private jet, called on Sunday for the tactics to end and said he had not been fully informed by Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
"I hope (that the government) will choose a path and will continue on that path," Berlusconi, who was overcome by emotion at one point during the visit, told reporters.
"And that this blockade be suspended absolutely because it is hard to see where it is leading us to."
Berlusconi said the policy was badly thought out, risky and unworthy of a civilised country such as Italy.
"We have a Christian tradition that obliges us to provide shelter to whoever needs it," he added.
The former prime minister and media mogul said the tragedy in international waters had complicated the mission that Italy is preparing to lead into Albania.
"It will certainly make our mission in Albania more difficult because many Albanians will undoubtedly have negative feelings against us," he told reporters.

The multinational force is due to secure Vlore, the northern port of Durres and Tirana airport for supplies, running short after the unrest. Albania's crisis was sparked by protests at the failure of savings schemes since late 1996.
About 7,000 people protested in Vlore on Sunday with some demonstrators warning the Italians to stay away if they wanted to stay alive.
Junior Foreign Minister Piero Fassino countered Berlusconi's remarks, saying the tragedy must not be exploited by politicians.

"It is truly alarming that Berlusconi should go and cry in Brindisi when a large number of Forza Italia members have in recent days constantly accused the government of being too benevolent and permissive," he countered.

"And it is even more alarming that a section of the political class should abandon themselves to this sort of exploitation at a time when thousands of our boys are leaving for Albania on a humanitarian mission of peace.
"This all risks creating a hostile climate around our men," Fassino said.
"What happened in the Straits of Otranto cannot hide the fact that Italy has given shelter in a civilised fashion to almost 13,000 Albanians in just a few days."
The government insisted Prodi had told Berlusconi what the navy was doing in a telephone conversation on Thursday and said the opposition leader was "in complete agreement."
